releases.name: v0.7.0: per-session worktrees
releases.body:
## What is new since 0.6.0

- Each OpenCode session starts its Muse session on a server-managed worktree instead of sharing the checkout, so concurrent sessions stop serializing at the workspace lock (tracks #34, which stays open for the remaining lease-protocol and orphans work).
- The human merges through normal source control; the bridge never auto-merges, and purge-on-close removes only provably-empty worktrees.
- Graceful fallback: untrusted workspaces and CLIs without the experimental surface keep the single-writer lock with a conversational notice.
- First-turn labels tell the agent which worktree it is on; PDF staging follows the session onto its worktree.

Strict build, 310/310 tests, and package-contents checks pass. Install snippet pinned to 0.7.0 in the same commit (lockstep rule).

releases.name: v0.6.0: audio transcription and PDF staging
releases.body:
## What is new since 0.5.2

- Audio attachments are transcribed in-plugin through `muse voice transcribe` (voice mode is subscription-included) and enter the turn as declared labeled text; untranscribable clips fail loudly, never silently dropped (#32, closed).
- PDF attachments are staged into `<workspace>/.opencode-muse-uploads/<uuid>.pdf` for the agent to read with its own tools; staged names are always generated, retention is purge-on-close (#33, closed).
- Install snippet pinned to 0.6.0 in the same commit (lockstep rule).

No changes to approvals, billing lane, or session management. Strict build, 301/301 tests, and package-contents checks pass.

releases.name: v0.5.2: install snippet matches release
releases.body: Docs-only follow-up: the README install snippet now names opencode-muse@0.5.2 in the same commit as the version bump, so the npm page never points at an older plugin. No code changes; strict build and 284/284 tests pass.

releases.name: v0.5.1: README refresh
releases.body: Docs-only release so the npm package page reflects the 0.5.0 functionality: conversational approvals (#30) and option-question answers (#31) are now claimed as Features, Contributor-by-default is stated up front, and Current limitations keeps only genuine residuals. No code changes since v0.5.0; strict build and 284/284 tests pass.

releases.name: v0.5.0: conversational option-question answers
releases.body:
## What is new since 0.4.0

- Conversational answers for structured option-questions (#31, closed): userInput/request parks in a per-session exchange instead of failing with method-not-found; the oldest unanswered question renders as a lettered list and the next message answers it (exact-one-match, re-ask once then cancel with a reason). Multi-select and option-less questions cancel with a named reason. userInputDialogs stays false so honoring servers see no behavior change.

## Known limitations (unchanged)

- Rewind/fork is unavailable on the pinned Linux runtime (tracked in #20, upstream bug filed).
- Provider approvals depend on core support (tracked in #22, upstream feature request filed); the conversational workaround in #30 stands in meanwhile.
- Structured input beyond single-select option-questions cancels with a reason (tracked in #6, upstream support awaited).
- Live event-gap recovery is unverified; fake-host coverage stands in (tracked in #23, closed as unobservable).

Strict build, 284/284 tests, and package-contents checks pass on the tag via the publish workflow.
